source.name: Spicer Designs Hair Salon HTML template
source.rightsEvidence: The official source page states CC BY 4.0 and commercial use with the footer credit retained. The downloaded package includes its LICENSE and README, which identify the bundled hero artwork as AI-generated placeholder art and require keeping the Spicer Designs footer link.

provenance.attribution: The unmodified source HTML retains the required linked Spicer Designs footer credit, visible in both captures. Any future adaptation or derivative must preserve attribution and must not suggest endorsement.
provenance.capture: Rendered locally from the exact official HTML archive at desktop 1440x1000 and mobile 390x844. Captures use the package's built-in prefers-reduced-motion static fallback so all scroll-reveal content is visible. Source files were not edited.
provenance.qa: Body and document widths matched the viewport at desktop and mobile. The sole bundled hero image loaded. The static HTML has no reveal observer: 18 hs-rise groups remain hidden in the default motion preference, while reduced motion exposes them. FAQ uses native details; click-driven widgets are presentational and forms have no submit destination.

referenceDna.annotatedDescription: A dark, warm salon experience built around planning a visit rather than a vague beauty promise. A slim booking/phone utility bar precedes a cinematic salon-interior hero with two direct actions. The central service menu is a price-and-time matrix with columns for stylist levels, followed by a clear explanation of stylist tiers. Colour work takes a separate consultation and patch-test route. Product recommendations, a gallery policy, short proof, native FAQ, and a focused appointment form complete the page. The source intends Inter and Fraunces, but its generated font utility maps the custom font token to font-weight rather than font-family, so the capture appears system-sans; implement font roles correctly if adopting the intended pair.

heroGeometry.mode: cinematic salon interior with concise service promise
heroGeometry.alignment: dark image-backed hero with left-aligned headline and two compact actions; thin appointment and telephone bar above
heroGeometry.viewport: phone/booking utility, service promise, and booking/menu actions occupy the first desktop screen

navigationGeometry.mode: small wordmark and plain section links
navigationGeometry.placement: inside the hero beneath a narrow utility bar
navigationGeometry.mobile: utility/phone remains readable, section links collapse or wrap, hero actions stack without obscuring the headline

typography.display: intended Fraunces editorial face, though static HTML currently falls back to system sans
typography.body: intended Inter neutral sans, though font-family utility is miscompiled in the capture
typography.scale: large two-line promise, compact uppercase mono-like labels, dense but readable service table

palette.contrastIntent: moody salon atmosphere with high-contrast booking actions and readable table content

imageTreatment.mode: atmospheric salon-interior hero image with layered dark gradients
imageTreatment.crop: wide hero image under left-to-right and bottom gradients; all later sections rely mostly on typography, tables, and lists
imageTreatment.focalPoint: salon environment rather than a person; use only client-owned, licensed, or newly generated imagery

servicePresentation.pattern: service matrix with a duration column and separate price by stylist level; colour services are routed through a consultation qualification instead of immediate booking
servicePresentation.interaction: a colour-only filter button is presentational in the HTML archive; reproduce it only if a working filter is implemented, with a complete static menu fallback

ctaPlacement.primary: appointment request in the hero and again in the final focused form
ctaPlacement.secondary: service-menu jump link beside hero action
ctaPlacement.early: before the service matrix, with consultation qualification placed before any color booking

motion.primitive: small section-rise reveals and native FAQ disclosures
motion.library: CSS transitions in the static package; no reveal observer is included in the HTML build
motion.reducedMotion: make all content visible without transforms; this fallback was used for captures

rules: keep telephone and booking access above the first section
turn the service matrix into stacked service rows that retain duration and level pricing
present stylist tiers as labeled blocks instead of shrinking columns
keep the colour consultation path separate and visible
stack form fields and preserve full-width touch actions without horizontal overflow

prohibitedPatterns: copying Spicer branding, sample salon name, source text, hero image, placeholder business, or footer attribution out of a derivative
reusing demo prices, staff names, service times, reviews, color rules, or business hours as client facts
inventing stylist credentials, price levels, appointment availability, allergy advice, patch-test timing, or color safety claims
presenting AI-generated room art as the client's real premises
leaving the static reveal groups invisible
pretending the static HTML filter or form submits
generic service-card wall or late-only appointment action

requiredSignatureElements.description: a slim phone or booking utility above the cinematic salon opening
a service menu that exposes duration and verified price variation by stylist level
a separate consultation or patch-test booking path only when required by verified salon policy
a clear, minimal appointment request form with a truthful submission route

acceptanceChecks: desktop and mobile preserve the price/time/stylist-level relationship
mobile service menu has no horizontal overflow
booking and consultation routes are operational and use client tokens
all prices, timing, staff credentials, color policies, and reviews are verified
reveal elements remain visible if animation JavaScript is unavailable
fonts use explicit font-family rules and have a readable fallback
CC BY footer attribution remains linked in any adapted template

review.scope: Official package/license, single AI-generated hero asset, Google Fonts OFL metadata, local full-page renders, attribution, and responsive inspection.
